entries.reason: Desktop renderer/typecheck/Electron E2E exact-head CI contract. iOS does not reuse Electron jobs; replacement evidence is .github/workflows/ios-desktop-main-architecture.yml plus ios-desktop-main-completeness.yml and protected-session UI acceptance. Desktop workflow remains an upstream verification dependency, not iOS shipping code.

PR20-era Grok reference import workflow with write access to the old Desktop migration branch. It is not an iOS runtime/build dependency. iOS replacement is live Desktop-main authority/rebaseline in ios-desktop-main-architecture.yml; no source-import automation is inherited.

PR20-era workflow that tested Desktop Host Rust then mutated the old architecture manifest. iOS must not inherit that manifest promotion mechanism; replacement is current exact-head Rust Host/iOS-owned module gates in ios-desktop-main-architecture.yml and completeness acceptance.
Old PR20 architecture inventory/renderer verification workflow. It has no iOS shipping role; current iOS authority and build/test gates replace it and must stay tied to final exact HEAD.

Desktop macOS signing/notarization/installer/updater acceptance is platform-specific. iOS release replacement is ios-store-delivery.yml plus ios-desktop-main-completeness.yml archive/signing/device/TestFlight/App Store gates; product/release semantics remain required but macOS packaging steps are not copied.

Desktop canonical Rust Host/Coordinator/Runner and runtime CI is relevant as upstream behavior evidence, but its macOS/desktop graph is not directly runnable on iOS. Replacement is the iOS architecture rust-host job and completeness Rust/device gates against iOS-owned sources. Current 92fcc2b0 delta now exercises the Mahayana platform-worker RCS server contract; iOS uses its own exact-head architecture/protected-session workflows while this remains an upstream verification dependency.

Desktop TDRP exact-origin/external-auth privilege test is a security dependency. iOS replacement is source/shared/external-url-policy.swift plus first-party auth sanitation in Rust product owner and focused SharedSettingsParityTests/current exact-head Actions; Electron ownership checks are platform-specific.

TDRP Telegram source-authority/inventory workflow governs a separate Desktop migration project and its upstream lock. It is not an iOS product runtime dependency. Any product responsibilities that land in canonical Desktop main are independently captured by the iOS Desktop-main authority inventory; no Telegram authority state is inherited.

Desktop canonical Search replacement/dedupe CI carries a product responsibility, not a reusable iOS workflow. iOS must satisfy the corresponding native search responsibility through current ledger rows, focused Swift/UI tests and final exact-head completeness evidence.

Repository-wide Desktop spec-first/existing-owner/exact-evidence governance was read as active upstream process context. iOS follows its own AGENTS.md/current parity Spec while preserving these applicable discipline requirements; this file is not copied as production code.

Declares Desktop automation client operations status/snapshot/find/action/wait/assert and cancellation. iOS replacement is the native FabushiAppAgentSurface and its focused tests/protected journeys; Desktop loopback discovery file and fabushi.desktop appId are platform-specific.

Implements private bounded loopback discovery, bearer-token calls, operation allowlist, response limits, timeout/cancellation and unavailable projection for Desktop automation. iOS uses native FabushiAppAgentSurface/Coordinator boundaries and protected-account UI acceptance rather than a local filesystem/loopback HTTP discovery channel; the security properties remain required in native form.

Defines cross-platform auth/runtime/chat/marketplace/MiniApp/capability-approval/interrupt/session-clear journeys. These are applicable product acceptance responsibilities; iOS replacement is current protected Global Dharma/session workflows plus native UI/runtime tests. The contract is not waived even though action drivers differ.

Documents Desktop restored monorepo dependencies and provenance needed for standalone Desktop builds. iOS must independently account for responsibilities from those restored sources through the 7,950-row ledger and its own repository-owned implementations; Desktop checkout coupling is not allowed.

Desktop test proves the shipping Agent Network is reached through the authenticated workspace and remains responsive to real zoom/navigation. iOS replacement is FabushiAgentNetworkView.swift plus MobileAgentNetworkParityTests.swift, which cover feature-gate availability, graph/activity semantics, account/reconnect stale-result fencing, bounded scale/layout and native accessibility/open-target behavior. Electron/browser-login harness details are platform-specific; product behavior remains applicable.

Desktop test proves the packaged semantic App MCP has bounded snapshots, sensitive-value redaction, generation fencing, action/assert behavior and private publication. iOS replacement is FabushiAppAgentSurface.swift and FabushiAppAgentSurfaceTests.swift: fabushi.app status/snapshot/find/action/wait/assert, bounded element count, sensitive value omission, stale-generation rejection and deterministic find/assert are native shipping contracts. Desktop loopback discovery transport is not copied.

Desktop test proves plaintext remains opaque, cancelled edits do not persist, OS-backed encryption is required, rotation/listing do not expose secret values, and storage fails closed when secure encryption is unavailable. iOS carries the underlying secret-storage responsibility in repository-owned Mahayana secrets/keyring code and native secret validation; exact iOS UI/Keychain shipping-entrypoint evidence still requires independent ledger closure, so this file is reviewed as an active dependency contract rather than treated as complete.

Desktop journey proves assistant semantic projection survives real workspace navigation/search/channel transitions and exposes the correct assistant/unread App Surface state. This is an applicable product responsibility on iOS; native App Agent Surface plus messaging projection owners and focused tests replace the Electron journey. Exact native end-to-end assistant/unread journey evidence remains required before product closure.

Desktop transport contract requires authoritative conversation.list refresh after conversation open and assistant completion so unread state is not stale. iOS repository-owned messaging core has actor-scoped unread/read-cursor persistence and reload tests, while native runtime projection must consume that authority. The Electron transport implementation is platform-specific; the refresh/projection invariant remains an active iOS requirement.

Desktop test proves the shipping avatar surface is bounded to a finite runtime state and that the retired Grok motion CSS/DOM runtime is absent. iOS compiles frontend/src/recovered/features/agent-info/ClothGhostAvatar.swift and frontend/src/production/MobileOnboardingCharacter.swift into the Fabushi target; both use one native vector TimelineView, honor accessibilityReduceMotion, and MobileAgentAvatar projects the canonical MobileBotSummary avatar state. The native state vocabulary is not a one-for-one copy of Desktop (iOS currently exposes idle/thinking/searching/working/loading/sending/orbit), so the file is reviewed but exact state/effect parity plus focused final-HEAD UI evidence remain open.

Desktop umbrella acceptance exercises the single Fabushi Messenger/Agent product root, transcript/runtime ownership, prompt references, sidebar layout, recovery and Host event projection. iOS production replacements are the compiled GrokMobileShell family, GrokMobileBotService, canonical Coordinator/Host/Runner sources, MobileAgentSidebarSections and repository-owned messaging/runtime modules with focused Swift/Rust tests. Because this one test spans many selected-ledger responsibilities, it is reviewed as an active product contract and must not be treated as source/runtime closure until those responsibilities and same-HEAD end-to-end evidence are individually closed.

Desktop test captures packaged Electron visual evidence for signed-in navigation, search/settings, assistant conversation and a real send/response. Electron selectors and screenshot geometry are platform-specific. iOS replacement is the native SwiftUI shipping surface compiled from frontend/** plus the final simulator/physical-device, iPhone/iPad, accessibility and release evidence required by ios-desktop-main-completeness.yml. Product journey parity remains required; this row is reviewed, not verified.

Desktop test is a multi-domain shipping contract for one Hermes-style assistant turn, Human reply/attachment/reaction/search/forward durability, two-device convergence, localization/accessibility/IME, Human calls, restart/handoff and self-hosted Bot invocation without impersonation. iOS has native owners across MessagingModel.swift, HumanCallsView.swift and call adapters, GrokMobileBotService/Coordinator/Host, plus ForwardMessageParityTests, MobileUiPreferencesLocalizationParityTests and messaging/runtime tests. Exact protected/native end-to-end coverage of every sub-journey is still required, so this umbrella file is reviewed but not closed.

Desktop regressions cover terminal-vs-transient auth classification, Mini App separation/routing, composer viewport containment, dynamic avatar continuity and narrow-layout conversation info. iOS native replacements exist in account/auth owners, GlobalDharma/MiniApp surfaces, GrokMobileShell SwiftUI layout, MobileAgentAvatar/ClothGhostAvatar and ConversationInfoView. The contracts remain applicable on iPhone/iPad and require focused UI/protected evidence before closure.

Desktop Messenger acceptance spans unified navigation, Router/settings/usage/sandbox preferences, logout/cache isolation, local-first lists, channel/group creation, Mini App discovery, per-peer drafts/search and anti-impersonation at the Host boundary. iOS implements corresponding native product owners in GrokMobileShell*, MessagingModel, ChatSearchModel, MarketplaceModel, MiniApp/WebMCP surfaces, account/session code and the repository-owned Host/Runner graph, with many focused tests. This broad file remains an umbrella contract until each selected responsibility and same-final-HEAD UI/service evidence is independently verified.

Desktop proves the Global Dharma Bot/WebMCP/UI/account/payment/restore journey stays inside one host boundary without token exposure. iOS shipping replacements are GlobalDharmaMiniAppView.swift, GlobalDharmaMiniAppBridge.swift, MiniAppWebMcpSurface.swift, GlobalDharmaCommerceModel.swift/FabushiPayStoreKit.swift and the protected GlobalDharma UI journey. These sources are compiled into the app and have focused tests, but real protected-account/service/commerce evidence must still succeed on the same final HEAD before this responsibility can be verified.

Desktop contract requires the official Global Dharma Mini App to be discoverable, installable/openable and placed coherently next to the composer entry. iOS has native MarketplaceModel, command/search surfaces, GlobalDharmaMiniAppView and Bot/Mini App production wiring. Desktop DOM placement is not copied, but equivalent native discovery/install/open UX and final iPhone/iPad evidence remain required.

Desktop test binds one coworker identity/shape across roster, header action, completed transcript step and final peer message while enforcing bounded desktop geometry. iOS preserves canonical agent identity through MobileBotSummary, MobileAgentAvatar/ClothGhostAvatar and GrokMobileShell projections; native phone/tablet geometry is platform-adapted. Identity continuity and final native UI evidence remain open, so this is reviewed rather than marked complete.

The Electron signed-candidate launcher/CDP/package mechanics are not applicable to iOS as an implementation. Their release responsibility is replaced by ios-desktop-main-completeness.yml plus ios-store-delivery.yml, signed archive/export, clean physical-device install/launch, upgrade, TestFlight/App Store and artifact-provenance gates. The underlying Agent/network/plugin/lifecycle product journeys remain applicable and are tracked in their native runtime/UI responsibilities; this platform-specific harness is not evidence that those journeys are already closed.

Desktop source defines stable pinned/named/unassigned projection, exclusive assignment, reserved-id normalization and search expansion of collapsed groups. iOS production owner MobileAgentSidebarSections.swift is compiled and provides canonical normalization, exclusive agent assignment, custom section CRUD/reordering/collapse plus account-scoped fallback persistence, with MobileAgentSidebarSectionsTests. The exact synthetic pinned/unassigned section projection is not yet demonstrated by the native owner, so this row records a real parity gap and stays active.

Desktop smoke drives every declared Host journey through the unified UI, Host feature protocol, approvals/interrupts, Mini App and security boundary. iOS owns an equivalent Coordinator/Host/Runner graph, typed bridges, native Mini App surface and product UI; current architecture/rust-host workflows exercise many of those contracts. This is an umbrella cross-platform journey and remains pending until the final completeness/protected/device evidence proves all applicable declared journeys on one exact HEAD.

Desktop test covers unified Messenger plus Electron native-menu routing, browser-auth lifecycle and safe native reads. Electron menu/process mechanics are replaced on iOS by SwiftUI scene/navigation, account/auth adapters, URL/deep-link policy and typed native services compiled into the app. The underlying auth cancellation/reopen, single product root and safe-read semantics remain applicable; native lifecycle/device evidence is still required.

Desktop contract requires duplicate participant rows to collapse to one canonical identity using the newest replacement, including hidden/visible replacement semantics. iOS GrokMobileCommandPaletteModel.entries deduplicates canonical bot rows and its focused test testDuplicateBotRosterKeepsOriginalSlotButUsesNewestCanonicalRow proves newest data replaces the stale row while retaining stable ordering. Human/contact canonical-search projection still needs exact end-to-end confirmation, so this file is reviewed but not globally verified.

Desktop security contract strips foreign tgWebAuth/autologin credentials even under casing/encoding tricks, preserves server-accepted auth URLs only for the exact first-party origin, rejects credential-bearing or scheme-mismatched auth URLs, and allowlists safe non-HTTP schemes. iOS compiles source/shared/external-url-policy.swift in the Fabushi target and implements the same sanitization/origin checks with URLComponents. A dedicated focused XCTest for these exact attack cases is not present yet, so production replacement exists but final verification remains open.

Electron/Vite HTML bootstrap owns desktop-only CSP/root mounting and renderer stylesheet linkage. iOS does not ship an HTML renderer shell; replacement is the native SwiftUI application target rooted at mobile/ios/Fabushi/FabushiApp.swift and mobile/ios/project.yml. Equivalent security/product effects are enforced through iOS native navigation/WebView boundaries and ATS; final exact-head UI/security acceptance remains required.

Locks the Electron/Vite/Playwright/Node dependency graph for the desktop package. iOS must not reuse that runtime graph; replacement dependency/build authority is mobile/ios/project.yml with pinned Swift packages plus iOS-owned Rust crates. Release provenance and license closure remain required under IOS-MAIN-AC-19.

Defines Desktop Electron runtime/build/package scripts, desktop app identity/protocol, native permission text, extra resources and macOS/Windows/Linux packaging. iOS replacement is mobile/ios/project.yml plus iOS-owned Rust prebuild, com.ombhrum.fabushi URL scheme/permission strings, ios-desktop-main-architecture.yml, ios-desktop-main-completeness.yml and ios-store-delivery.yml. Desktop JIT/Electron packaging is not copied; same product effects and release gates remain required.

Configures Desktop Playwright Electron/browser E2E execution, traces/screenshots/video and CI serialization. iOS replacement is the FabushiTests/FabushiUITests targets in mobile/ios/project.yml plus protected-account/completeness GitHub Actions and xcresult/artifact evidence. Playwright itself has no iOS shipping role.

Product-owned Desktop visual styling for messenger shell, search, message/composer/info/settings/marketplace surfaces, agent-state accents and reduced-motion behavior. iOS does not reuse CSS; replacement is the native SwiftUI shipping shell and platform accessibility/motion behavior. Functional and visual parity, Dynamic Type/VoiceOver/localization/reduced-motion evidence remains pending final exact-head IOS-MAIN-AC-13 acceptance.

Desktop package icon asset. iOS replacement is mobile/ios/Fabushi/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset with iPhone/iPad/App Store icon variants selected by ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME in mobile/ios/project.yml. Final signed archive/TestFlight/App Store identity evidence remains required.

macOS hardened-runtime Electron JIT/unsigned-executable-memory entitlements are platform-specific and must not be copied to iOS. iOS replacement is mobile/ios/Fabushi/Fabushi.entitlements plus platform capabilities declared by the iOS target; final signing/entitlement validation remains required.

Mac App Store inherited sandbox/JIT entitlements for Electron child processes are macOS-specific. Native iOS has no Electron child-process inheritance or JIT requirement; replacement capability boundary is the signed iOS app/extension entitlements and sandbox, including the broadcast extension where applicable.

Mac App Store sandbox/network/files/microphone/camera plus Electron JIT entitlements are Desktop MAS packaging contracts. iOS replacement uses Apple-native sandbox/permission prompts, mobile/ios/Fabushi/Fabushi.entitlements, project.yml usage descriptions/background modes and app-extension entitlements. Final store signing/privacy/entitlement acceptance is still pending.

Desktop-only static/UI contract verifies OpenBot/Grok skin activation, deterministic BotMark identity, thinking/action/result transcript projection, structured assistant result surfaces and message actions. iOS does not execute this Node script; equivalent product responsibilities live in native SwiftUI messaging/agent surfaces and must be covered by iOS unit/UI/accessibility tests on the final exact HEAD. Visual identity/reduced-motion acceptance remains pending IOS-MAIN-AC-13.

Bundles Electron main/preload and the Rust Coordinator carrier with esbuild for Node/Electron. iOS must not ship Electron or this bundle graph; replacement is the native Xcode target in mobile/ios/project.yml plus iOS-owned Rust prebuild through scripts/build-mahayana-ios.sh and the iOS architecture workflow.

Fail-closed Desktop architecture gate enforces Renderer -> Electron -> Coordinator -> Host -> Runner, single production roots, durable runtime state, capability audit and recovery. iOS replacement is scripts/check-desktop-main-ios-architecture.py plus ios-desktop-main-architecture.yml, with Swift/native adapters replacing Electron while preserving Coordinator/Host/Runner and single-owner constraints.

Desktop App Agent contract keeps stale-generation actions fail-closed, allows only bounded identity-stable rebasing and forbids positional/route/screen drift. iOS native replacement is mobile/ios/Fabushi/FabushiAppAgentSurface.swift, which owns generation-scoped snapshots/actions and stale_app_surface_generation failure, together with focused App Agent surface tests/current exact-head CI. No Electron DOM rebasing layer is copied.

Scans emitted Electron renderer assets for forbidden legacy runtime/UI markers. iOS has no emitted Vite renderer bundle; replacement is source/architecture closure against the native SwiftUI shipping composition and final Xcode archive, enforced by iOS architecture/completeness workflows rather than text scanning an Electron dist tree.

Validates the co-staged Electron main/preload/Coordinator carrier/renderer artifact graph and app-host binary wiring. iOS replacement is the signed native app/archive graph produced from mobile/ios/project.yml with linked iOS-owned Rust runtime and verified by architecture, device-archive, completeness and store-delivery gates. Electron parentPort/app-host staging mechanics are not applicable.

Electron/Playwright diagnostic probes renderer bootstrap, native/runtime bridges, auth/onboarding progression, persistence and canonical conversation/bot/group runtime hydration with bounded waits. iOS replacement is native protected-account/UI acceptance plus runtime status/projection tests on the shipping SwiftUI app; Electron window/DOM probing is not reused.

macOS CI evidence recorder validates a playable screen-capture movie with fail-closed runner/display probes. iOS does not use macOS screencapture/host display drivers; replacement evidence comes from iOS UI test xcresult/screenshots/video where available plus physical-device/TestFlight acceptance artifacts in completeness/store-delivery. The requirement for inspectable visual evidence remains.

AVFoundation helper encodes/validates macOS session-recorder frames into a playable H.264 movie. It is test-evidence tooling, not product runtime. iOS replacement is native XCTest/xcresult/device evidence collection; this exact macOS frame encoder has no shipping iOS responsibility.

Re-signs nested macOS Host/ASR binaries with canonical identifiers, seals the Electron app and optionally submits/staples Apple notarization. iOS replacement is native code signing/export/TestFlight/App Store delivery in ios-store-delivery.yml and completeness gates; macOS notarization/stapling and Developer ID nested binary mechanics are not copied.

Copies Desktop Host, Coordinator and box-exec executables into Electron resources/bin after Rust builds. iOS preserves Coordinator/Host/Runner responsibilities but links/builds iOS-owned Rust through scripts/build-mahayana-ios.sh and Xcode project settings; no sidecar executable staging is permitted/needed on iOS.

Desktop component test checks grouped agent steps/operation isolation/stopped state, explicit complete-HTML Mini App affordance, inert unsafe Markdown and Mini App result cards. iOS replacement is native Bot/Agent conversation and Mini App Swift/XCTest/UI coverage through the shipping surfaces; the React SSR harness itself is platform-specific.

Desktop TypeScript compiler configuration for Fabushi account policy/service contract tests. iOS equivalent account/product contracts live in iOS-owned Rust/Swift targets and are built/tested by Cargo/Xcode in GitHub Actions; this TS compilation mechanism is not applicable.

TypeScript contract compilation set covering Desktop shared/Electron/preload/update/MCP/local-exec boundaries. Each applicable product responsibility is tracked in selected-source ledgers and mapped to native iOS/Rust owners; the Electron TypeScript compilation aggregate itself is replaced by Rust/Swift architecture/build/test gates.

Desktop React/Vite renderer TypeScript configuration, aliases and production entry coverage. iOS uses Swift 6/XcodeGen project configuration and native source roots; React/Vite typechecking is not an iOS build dependency, while underlying product responsibilities remain in the source ledger.

Desktop Vite/React renderer bundling, aliases, dev server and dist output configuration. Native iOS ships no Vite renderer bundle; replacement is the Xcode application target and native SwiftUI composition in mobile/ios/project.yml. Mini App/Web content remains separately controlled by its native WebMCP/WebView owners.

Desktop ADR is a proposed/no-production-implementation decision record, but it defines a mandatory independent settlement owner whenever Fabushi enables paid entitlements, purchases, credits or transferable value. iOS already ships commerce, so this is applicable architecture rather than N/A. Current iOS replacement is repository-owned Rust payment/ledger/settlement code (including mahayana-platform-core payment_infra and mahayana-messaging settlement verification) composed with FabushiPayStoreKit and GlobalDharmaCommerceModel. The native path preserves trusted catalog/amount identity, idempotency, provider verification, account binding and server-authoritative entitlement projection; final real-service, signed App Store/restore, device and exact-head release evidence remains required and this review does not mark commerce verified.

Desktop ADR is proposed/no-production-implementation but defines the required independent CallSession/Signaling owner if calls exist. Calls are active in the iOS product, so the responsibility is applicable. iOS replacement uses the repository-owned Rust source/host/extensions/session/call-session.rs durable call/session and ordered signaling store with generation fencing, plus HumanCallSystemCoordinator (CallKit/PushKit), HumanCallMediaPort, HumanCallPeerConnection and the unified HumanCallsView surface. The active ios-human-call-media-parity spec preserves canonical Host ownership, reconnect/resume, media/device projection and stale-callback fencing. Real two-device media/background/push/device acceptance and final exact-head release evidence remain open, so this review is not a verified claim.

Desktop architecture reference records owner-level lessons from bhrumom/fabu (Agent identity/profile separation, per-turn ownership, bounded inference context, progress/cancellation/approval/checkpoint semantics and per-Agent concurrency). It is not a standalone shipping dependency and does not override current Desktop main. iOS preserves the applicable product responsibilities through its current Coordinator/Host/Runner, repository-owned Rust runtime/session/memory/permission/scheduler owners and SwiftUI presentation. Any responsibility that is shipping in current Desktop main remains accounted for in the selected ledger and must earn exact-head production evidence there; reference-only follow-up wording is not promoted to completed work.

Active Desktop FBCP-001 Revision 7 is an upstream product/architecture requirement, not a runtime asset. It requires complete responsibility/source closure, existing-owner-first composition, one canonical product root, service-backed communication/calls/payments/search/accessibility/recovery and exact-head GitHub Actions evidence. iOS preserves these applicable invariants through the canonical Desktop-main iOS parity spec and selected 7,950-row responsibility ledger; no historical Desktop acceptance or Telegram network implementation is inherited. This review records the requirement source only and does not promote any iOS responsibility to verified.

Active Desktop parity/recovery spec documents the architecture boundaries and failure modes that produced current Fabushi owners: Rust-owned execution/durable state, typed pushed runtime events, bounded provider progress/cancellation, MCP product completeness, low-power lifecycle and exact packaged evidence. Its old Grok/PR baselines are provenance, not current iOS authority. Applicable responsibilities are independently represented by current Desktop-main source rows and iOS Coordinator/Host/Runner, MCP, runtime projection and lifecycle owners; historical completion claims are not inherited.

Active Desktop cutover spec defines sole Agent root, typed identity, Rust-owned conversation execution/durable state, CapabilityBroker, ComputerControlLease, event-driven power behavior, design-system discipline and exact-source/release gates. PR #14/version-specific release sequencing is historical Desktop process, while the owner boundaries remain relevant architecture provenance. iOS maps the applicable boundaries into its native SwiftUI + Coordinator/Host/Runner + repository-owned Rust composition and must prove them through current ledgers and exact-head Actions; this document itself has no iOS shipping code.

RCS-01..10 defines server/mobile control-session creation reconciliation. Current iOS shipping does not call /v1/computers/:device_id/sessions; its Remote Computer product path is RemoteComputerSurface -> IOSPreloadBridge -> IOSMainRuntime -> MahayanaCoordinator -> canonical Host plus restricted official WebView/VNC. FabushiRemoteDeviceGateway is separately account-token authenticated and must not be repurposed as a mobile control token/Runner bearer. The upstream Worker contract remains a service dependency and aggregate owners/callers still require review.

Generic Desktop specification-authoring template only; it carries no runtime, product state or release asset. Its governance intent (explicit ownership, contracts, failure modes, verification and evidence) is replaced by the iOS repository AGENTS/current Desktop-main parity spec and task-specific native specs. No production code is copied and no user capability is waived.

Repository-wide Desktop Spec-first/No-Spec-No-Code governance. It carries no runtime responsibility but requires durable requirements, ownership, failure modes, verification and evidence before product-affecting implementation. iOS applies the same discipline through its AGENTS.md, current Desktop-main parity spec and task-specific native specs; no product capability is waived.

Desktop audit records the canonical structured-log facade and producer-to-Host ownership for runtime/queue/tool/MCP/Box/turn diagnostics, including redaction, typed event mapping and exact-head evidence. iOS does not copy the Desktop JSONL/Electron transport, but observability, secret redaction, unique runtime owner and diagnostic settlement are applicable responsibilities and remain tracked in the selected ledger/native runtime telemetry owners. Historical per-commit green evidence in this audit is provenance only and cannot satisfy current iOS exact-head acceptance.

Only responsibilities that actually land in canonical bhrumom/fabushi-desktop@main enter the iOS Desktop-main inventory/ledger and are reimplemented in iOS-owned owners. The contract's existing-owner-first, single-root, typed-capability, service/recovery/security and evidence principles are relevant governance context, but TDRP status is not an iOS completion signal.
